answer.heading: My research conclusion
answer.text: Historical ITOT observations over the stated holding period show all 502 overlapping 36-month windows ended positive (worst +12.77%, best +93.34%), but past performance cannot guarantee your home down payment will be protected or that losses during the holding period will stay within an acceptable range. Without a decided loss limit, history cannot confirm whether observed drawdowns or potential future declines would disrupt your goal.

answer.heading: What supports this view
answer.text: Every historical 36-month window for ITOT finished positive, with the worst rolling 36-month return at +12.77%. The terminal loss over the full observed period was 0.00%, meaning ITOT never closed below its inception price.

answer.heading: What argues against it
answer.text: ITOT experienced a maximum drawdown requiring 714 calendar days to recover from its peak. The worst complete monthly return was -9.22%, and annualized observed volatility was 17.62%. These intra-period declines could force a sale below your purchase price if the home purchase cannot be delayed.

answer.heading: Important gaps and next step
answer.text: History cannot establish a future loss limit or whether the stated horizon aligns with your home down payment need if you lack flexibility to delay the purchase. The critical unknown is your acceptable loss threshold and whether you have reserve funds to cover shortfalls or postpone the home purchase if ITOT declines near your target date.
